SPECIFICATION FOR CALORIMETER THERMOMETERS
PART 2 ENCLOSED SCALE THERMOMETERS 1. scope - Prescribes the requirements for a series of short-range enclosed-scale calorimeter thermometers, graduated for vertical. total and Partial immersion, for use in bomb calorimetry and other purposes where an accurate measurement of change of temperature required, given in IS : 2627-1979 2 Terminology - For the purpose of this standard, the definitions `Glossary of terms relating to liquid-in-glass thermometer ( first revision )' shall apply. 3. Type The thermometers shall be of the mercury-in-glass enclosed-scale type ( see Fig, 1 ).

4.2 The thermometers shall preferably be calibrated for use at total immersion ( that is, the reading is taken when the thermometer is vertical and immersed at least to the end of the liquid column in the medium where temperature is required to be measured ). The calibration for use at partial immersion is permitted, if agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. On partial immersion thermometers, a line shall be etched at least half way round the stem of the thermometer at level to which it is intended to be immersed; which would preferably be the junction of the saddle and the sheath ( marked, E in Fig. 1 ). 5. 5.2.3 Strip bearing the scale - The strip bearing the scale shall be of a material suitable to the temperature to be measured and compatible with the method of fixing the strip. It shall be placed tightly against the capillary tube inside the sheath and shall be firmly and securely fastened at the top of the thermometer. A suitable method of fixing is by fusing a glass tube or rod to the sheath and to the upper end of the strip bearing the scale; the lower end of the strip shall be it shall be fixed inside the sheath in any other freely held in a suitable glass saddle. Alternatively, suitable manner that allows for differential expansion. tube shall be smooth. The cross-sectional 5.2 4 Capillary tube - The inside of the capillary area of the bore shall not show variations from the average greater than 5 percent and the bore shall be wide enough to ensure that, without tapping, jumping of the meniscus does not exceed one half of the graduation interval when the temperature is rising at a uniform rate not exceeding 0*05"C per minute. In the case of thermometers calibrated for use at partial immersion, the volume of mercury contained in the capillary tube betvveen the immersion line and the lowest figured scale line shall not exceed the equivalent of 2�C. 5.2.5 Expansion chamber ( safety chamber ) - The capillary tube shall have an enlargement at This expansion chamber the top of sufficient size to allow heating of the thermometer to 70%. shall be pear-shaped, with the hemisphere at the top. It shall be so shaped that the meniscus remains in the narrow portion at temperatures up to 4O'C. 5.2.6 Construction Chamber - A cotraction chamber shall be provided so that the mercury does not recede into the bulb at 0�C. It shall be elongated and as narrow as possible. *1 bar = 105 Pa 2

7. Accuracy
7.1 Scale Error - The scale error, when the thermometer is under normal atmospheric pressure and when the emergent liquid column ( in the case of a partial immersion thermometer ) is at the prescribed temperature, shall not be greater than 0.1 "C. 7.2 internal Error - The absolute value of the algebraic difference between the error at any two points which are not more than 50 divisions apart shall in no case be greater than O*Ol"C. 8. EXPLANATORY

NOTE calorimeter thermometers', issued

This standard is based on IS0 652-l 975 IEnclosed-scale by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ).

The calorimeters, not provided with auxiliary scales at O"C, are therefore not suited to the absolute measurement of temperature, unless they are checked against a standard thermometer immediately before use. The solid-stem calorimeter thermometers are covered in Part 1 of the standard. 4 Printed at printograph, New Delhi, lndie
